- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in the recent history, reduce forecasted peak values to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.3) in the recent history, increase forecasted lows to account for downward pressure.  
- When a recent price spike occurs (e.g., +1.5%+ in 3-5 days), model tends to overshoot — cap forecasted peaks at 10–15% below the immediate prior peak.  
- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon (especially days 1–7) — apply a 5–10% downward bias to first 7 days of forecast.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.0) and price is trending upward, model often fails to mean-revert — add a 3–5 day decay factor to forecasted values.  
- If sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward, model often underestimates the drop — apply a 5–10% upward bias to early forecasted lows.  
- Forecast errors are more pronounced when sentiment is volatile (±0.3 or higher) — use a smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) on sentiment to dampen extreme reactions.
